_source: Transcribed from Blood & Grit Player's Book v2.20, Ch. III–IV, VIII–X, XIII–XIV. Attack is derived from attackRank (Practiced=level, Steady=level-1, Slight=max(0,level-2)); saves are strong=2+level/2 or weak=level/3. Regenerate when those chapters change (see CLAUDE.md).

origins.name: The Banker
origins.line: A keeper of ledgers and a caller of notes, come west where the paper is thin and the interest is thick.
origins.boon: Money answers to you: you gain +2 on checks to appraise goods or find the trap in a contract. Once per session you may call in a favor of paper, a note or a lien or a letter of introduction, and have it honored by anyone who trades in credit.
origins.burden: The West remembers a foreclosure longer than a kindness; you take −2 on social checks with homesteaders, drovers, and the working poor, and there is a ledger somewhere with your name where a family's used to be.

origins.name: The Drover
origins.line: You brought cattle up the long trails out of Texas and slept in the saddle more nights than in a bed.
origins.boon: Stock answers you and the saddle never tires you: you gain +2 on checks to handle any animal, whether to calm it, drive it, or catch it. Once per scene you may ask a mount for more than it has and get it, at a cost the beast pays later.
origins.burden: Twelve years of shouting over a thousand head left you loud; you take −2 on Stealth, and you carry a voice that fills a room whether you mean it to or not.

origins.name: The Drummer
origins.line: A travelling seller of tonics, Bibles, futures, or lies.
origins.boon: Once per scene reroll a failed Persuade or Deceive; in any town of size, talk your way to a bed, a meal, or credit on your word alone.
origins.burden: Once a lie of yours is found out, those who caught it take −2 to trust you for the rest of the affair, and word travels ahead of you.

origins.name: The Fallen Gentry
origins.line: Once there was a name, a house, an inheritance — and then it was gone.
origins.boon: +2 on social checks among the wealthy, the lettered, and the powerful; you read rank and the lie beneath a fine coat at a glance.
origins.burden: −1 on Fortitude saves against plain hardships — hunger, exposure, hard labor.

origins.name: The Freed
origins.line: Born or sold into bondage, you took your own liberty and walked west.
origins.boon: +2 to read a stranger's true intent and on Will saves against being cowed; +2 to slip a bond or confinement — never quite cornered while any way out remains.
origins.burden: −1 on social checks with lawmen, soldiers, and officials, who feel your wariness and return it.

origins.name: The Gambler
origins.line: A living made, and lost, at the green-felt tables of a hundred towns.
origins.boon: A permanent +2 on Insight at any table; once per session reroll a single d20 and keep the better result.
origins.burden: When coin, cards, or a sure thing appear, the Keeper may call for a Will save to walk away — and old debts ride into town behind you.

origins.name: The Homesteader
origins.line: You broke sod that did not want breaking and buried more than one child under it.
origins.boon: A full night's rest in a camp you have made restores you and each companion an extra 1d6 Blood; your dogs and stock give warning before trouble arrives.
origins.burden: Away from home or kin, −1 on Initiative in the first round of any fight.

origins.name: The Laborer
origins.line: You laid rail, dug shafts, or drove spikes for wages that vanished at the company store.
origins.boon: +2 on Fortitude saves against fatigue, strain, and the wearing cold; you can labor or march long past where softer men fold.
origins.burden: −1 on checks of fine dexterity — sleight, lockwork, fuses, the surgeon's delicate art.

origins.name: The Madam
origins.line: You ran a house: the books, the peace, the safety of the women in it, and every secret that came through the door.
origins.boon: Nothing said in your parlor left it without your leave, and the habit stayed: once per session you may name one person of consequence in town and know a private truth about them. You gain +2 on checks to read what a person truly wants, and to hold a room without raising your voice.
origins.burden: Respectable folk will take your money and not your hand; you take −2 on social checks with the church-going and the office-holding, and a few of them work quietly to see you moved along.

origins.name: The Newspaperman
origins.line: You set type, chased stories, and kept a drawer of the ones no editor would run.
origins.boon: The clippings nobody believed are still yours: once per session you may declare your morgue file holds something on a person, a place, or a horror at hand, and learn one true thing about it. You gain +2 on checks to research a matter, or to get a stranger talking on the record.
origins.burden: You cannot leave a thing unasked, and your face asks before your mouth does; you take −1 on Deceive, and the Keeper may call for a Will save to keep a dangerous question behind your teeth.

origins.name: The Outlaw
origins.line: There is paper on you in at least one territory.
origins.boon: Once per session declare you have been somewhere before and know one useful, unsavory fact about it; +2 with criminals and fences, and +2 to make a quick exit when the law takes an interest.
origins.burden: Lawmen and bounty men take note of you; a warrant, a posse, or an old grudge may trail you into town.

origins.name: The Railroad Hand
origins.line: Grade, spike, wire, or timetable, you worked the line, and the country is a map of it to you.
origins.boon: The line still knows you: you ride freight or coach free wherever the rails run, and once per session a name from your working days opens a door, a boxcar, or a telegraph key. You gain +2 on any check to say where a rail or road or river runs.
origins.burden: The company's name rides with you; you take −2 on social checks with those the road took land or water or kin from, and there are men still on the payroll who would rather you had stayed on it.

origins.name: The Scout
origins.line: You read the land like scripture — guide, hunter, wagon-pilot.
origins.boon: Ignore difficult ground afoot and never be lost beneath an open sky; +2 on Notice against ambush, tracks, and lying-in-wait out of doors — never surprised under open sky.
origins.burden: Indoors and in close crowds you take −1 on Notice.

origins.name: The Undertaker
origins.line: You washed and boxed the dead of three towns, and not one of them frightened you until the day one sat up.
origins.boon: The dead are work to you and not horror: once per scene, when a corpse or a grave or a charnel sight would cost you Nerve, it costs you none. You gain +2 on Medicine to read what killed a body and how long it has lain there.
origins.burden: You have handled too many bodies to fear one, and that is exactly the trouble: the first time each session a corpse proves to be something other than a corpse, you are Off-Guard for a round while you finish deciding that it is.

origins.name: The Veteran
gear: Service carbine (1d10, Repeating — from your hitch)
origins.line: You served — blue or gray — and some of it wakes you in the small hours.
origins.boon: Once per session steady the line — you and each ally in earshot shrug off fear for a round; once per scene reroll a failed Reflex save to take cover.
origins.burden: First time each session sudden gunfire or the uncanny finds you, make a Dread Check or be Shaken a round.

origins.name: Came Back Wrong
origins.line: You died — and then you did not stay dead. You remember the dark on the other side.
origins.boon: Once per session, when you would drop to 0 Blood, stay standing at 1 until the end of the round; you need neither food nor sleep.
origins.burden: The Old Dark notices you first, and the living sense something wrong (−1 on first impressions with the breathing). You begin at Mark 1.

shapes.name: The Risen
shapes.hunger: Warmth, company, a reason to be upright.
shapes.feeding: A night of being treated as a person by somebody who knows what you are.
shapes.gift: You are hard to put down: your death threshold is twice your CON, and the blow that drops you leaves you on your feet until the end of the round it lands.

shapes.name: The Sanguine
shapes.feeding: You drink, and somebody is less afterward.
shapes.gift: What you take, you keep: when you feed, recover Blood as though you had mended, and pay no Hunger for it.

shapes.name: The Hollow
shapes.hunger: The memory you lost, and failing that, anyone else's.
shapes.feeding: You take a true memory from somebody willing to give it, and they do not get it back.
shapes.gift: You are not entirely here: once per scene, pass through a closed thing or let a blow pass through you.

shapes.name: The Tolled
shapes.hunger: Whatever the lender is asking this month.
shapes.feeding: You do the errand, and you do not get to know why.
shapes.gift: The lender answers: once per session ask for one thing within its reach and receive it, and take a Hunger for the asking.

edges.name: Quick Draw
edges.desc: Draw and Strike in one motion; +2 to the roll deciding who shoots first.

edges.name: Cylinder & Sky
edges.desc: Once per round, when you reduce a foe to 0 Blood, immediately spend an unused Beat to reload.

edges.name: Dead Eye
edges.desc: Once per scene, declare a Strike a hit short of the impossible: it cannot fail, and rolls damage twice keeping the higher.

edges.name: Fan the Hammer
edges.desc: With a single-action revolver, two Beats make up to three Strikes at half the usual Multiple Attack Penalty (−2/−4).

edges.name: Gunfighter's Calm
edges.desc: Once per scene, ignore the Multiple Attack Penalty on a single Strike.

edges.name: Practiced Reload
edges.desc: Reduce the Beats to reload a favored weapon by 1 (min 0); clear your own misfires as a single Interact.

edges.name: Steady Shot
edges.desc: If you do not move, ignore the first range increment penalty and gain +1 to hit; ignore Kickback recoil.

edges.name: Throw the Stick
edges.desc: If you carry powder, hurl a lit charge in place of a Strike.

edges.name: Two-Gun
edges.desc: A pistol in each hand; your off-hand Strike does not increase your Multiple Attack Penalty for the round.

edges.name: Fleet
edges.desc: Your Speed afoot increases by 10 feet.

edges.name: Hard to Kill
edges.desc: Once per session, when you would drop to 0 Blood, drop to 1 instead and stay on your feet.

edges.name: Iron Gut
edges.desc: +2 on Fortitude saves against poison, disease, drink, and spoiled provisions.

edges.name: Saddle-Born
edges.desc: Never fall from the saddle by mishap; fight mounted without penalty.

edges.name: Tough as Rawhide
edges.desc: Gain +1 Blood per level, now and as you advance.

edges.name: Born Lucky
edges.desc: Once per session, reroll any single roll you just made and keep the kinder result.

edges.name: Cold Read
edges.desc: +3 on Insight; spend a moment to learn one true thing a person is trying to hide.

edges.name: Gallows Humor
edges.desc: Once per scene, crack wise in the face of the awful and recover 1d6 Nerve — yours, or a companion's who laughs.

edges.name: Iron Will
edges.desc: Once per scene, reroll a failed save against fear, charm, or compulsion.

edges.name: Stone Nerve
edges.desc: +2 maximum Nerve per level and +1 on Dread Checks.

edges.name: Unshakable
edges.desc: The first time each scene you would lose Nerve, lose none instead.

edges.name: Dead Shot Provider
edges.desc: Never want for food or fresh horses where game or ranches exist; your camp is always well-sited.

edges.name: Frontier Medicine
edges.desc: Your field care heals an extra 1d6; improvise a remedy from what the land offers.

edges.name: Pathfinder
edges.desc: Never truly lost; +2 on overland travel; always find water, forage, and safe ground.

edges.name: Powder Sense
edges.desc: +2 to set, spot, or disarm charges and traps; your blasts never catch a friend you can plainly see.

edges.name: Tracker
edges.desc: +3 on Survival to track; track across stone, shallow water, and the spoor of unnatural things.

edges.name: Hedge Magic
edges.desc: Learn a single Sign and gain a small Nerve pool to fuel it, though you are not a Hexer.

edges.name: Salt-Wise
edges.desc: +2 on Lore (Occult); the Old Rites take you half the usual time and materials.

edges.name: Touched
edges.desc: Gain Witch-Sight, +1 Mark, and an unsettling certainty about where the dark is thickest.

edges.name: Warded
edges.desc: Scribe a ward at a threshold the uncanny cannot cross uninvited for a night.

edges.name: Two Guns Speaking
edges.desc: Both irons at once count as one Strike: roll once, and on a hit apply the damage of both weapons. Your Multiple Attack Penalty does not rise for it. Reloading two guns still takes reloading two guns.

edges.name: Through and Through
edges.desc: A shot that drops a foe carries on. When a Strike reduces a creature to 0 Blood, make one free Strike at the same attack against a second creature standing behind or beside it.

edges.name: The Last Round
edges.desc: You are never out at the moment it matters. Once per scene, declare that the chamber you thought was empty is not, and take one Strike with it at +2. Nobody has ever caught you counting.

edges.name: Old Bones, Old Habits
edges.desc: You do not get Fatigued, by weather, wounds, want of sleep, hard travel or the uncanny. You still feel all of it. You have simply stopped letting it decide anything.

edges.name: Get Up
edges.desc: Once per scene, on your own turn while Dying, stand at half your Blood with everything you were holding. Whatever put you down is entitled to be surprised.

edges.name: Nothing New Under the Sun
edges.desc: You have seen a version of this before. Gain +4 on any check to identify a creature, a working, a poison, a mechanism or a scheme, and the Keeper will tell you one true thing about it whether you rolled well or not.

edges.name: The Long View
edges.desc: Once per session, ask the Keeper what the worst likely consequence of the plan on the table is, and get a straight answer. It is not prophecy. It is thirty years of watching plans.

edges.name: The Country Knows You
edges.desc: You are never lost, never without water, and never without a place to sleep out of the weather, in any country you have crossed once before. Nothing hostile finds your camp by accident.

edges.name: Winter-Proof
edges.desc: Cold, heat, thin air, thirst, bad water and foul air do you no harm at all, and you may carry one soul through the same for a day.

edges.name: Bearing It
edges.desc: Your Mark does not show. No creature, holy ground, ward or gift of sight registers it, and it costs you none of its usual penalties in front of the living. It has all the same effects on what you are becoming.

edges.name: The Second Voice
edges.desc: Once per scene, work a Sign you know as a reaction rather than on your turn. Something in your throat does the speaking and it is not quite your accent.

edges.name: Known Far Off
edges.desc: Your name has travelled ahead of you. In any settlement, somebody already knows it and one of the following is true, your choice: they are glad, they are afraid, or they owe you. The Keeper says who.

callingEdges.name: Run It Down
callingEdges.desc: After a Bushwhack lands, immediately Step and Stride free; your quarry must spend an action to break away.

callingEdges.name: Devoted Unto Death
callingEdges.desc: Immune to fear of the power you serve; once per scene shrug off a wound's effect for a round.

callingEdges.name: Long Gone
callingEdges.desc: Once per scene, when no enemy is looking your way, slip from sight even while observed and take a free Stride into cover.

callingEdges.name: Charge Already Set
callingEdges.desc: Once per fight, declare that you prepared this ground before the shooting started. One explosive of yours is already placed where you now say it is, and goes off on your Beat.

callingEdges.name: Golden Tongue
callingEdges.desc: Work a single Deceive against an entire crowd at once.

callingEdges.name: Double or Nothing
callingEdges.desc: Once per scene, before you roll, name the stake: success is one degree better; failure one degree worse.

callingEdges.name: Pistolero's Tally
callingEdges.desc: When you drop a foe with a Strike, your next Strike this round ignores the Multiple Attack Penalty.

callingEdges.name: Hard Bargain
callingEdges.desc: Once per scene, work a Sign for one less Nerve than it asks; the unpaid cost comes due later.

callingEdges.name: The Long Arm
callingEdges.desc: When you Demoralize a foe or invoke the law against it, allies in earshot gain +1 on their next Strike against it.

callingEdges.name: Mending Hands
callingEdges.desc: Your remedies lift one lingering affliction along with the Blood they restore.

callingEdges.name: One Shot, One Kill
callingEdges.desc: Once per scene, a steadied shot against an unaware foe deals maximum Dead Aim dice and ignores hide or armor DR.

callingEdges.name: Shepherd's Word
callingEdges.desc: Spend a Beat to grant an ally in earshot an immediate save, with your bonus, against a fear already gripping them.

callingEdges.name: Hellfire Sermon
callingEdges.desc: Your invocations against the unclean reach every foe who can hear your voice.

callingEdges.name: Hang Fire
callingEdges.desc: Set a charge to blow on a trigger you name; it waits, patient as the deep.

callingEdges.name: Highball Charge
callingEdges.desc: Once per scene, overpack a charge: maximum dice and double burst radius.

callingEdges.name: Laid By
callingEdges.desc: Once per session, declare you laid by a useful mundane item, cache, or contact in this place — within reason, you did.

callingEdges.name: Battlefield Surgeon
callingEdges.desc: Field care in the thick of a fight provokes no reaction and restores an extra die of Blood.

callingEdges.name: Spirit-Spoken
callingEdges.desc: Once per scene, put one yes-or-no question to the spirits about this land, its dead, or what passed here, and be answered true.

callingEdges.name: Between Them and It
callingEdges.desc: When a foe would Strike an ally adjacent to you, you may take the Strike yourself instead. You are Off-Guard until your next turn, and the ally may not refuse.

callingEdges.name: Bitter Brew
callingEdges.desc: Keep one extra charm or poison prepared; your brews hold potency a full day longer.

callingEdges.name: Bane-Sharpened
callingEdges.desc: When you exploit your quarry's known weakness, deal an extra die of damage; name the kind of any uncanny thing on sight.

callingEdges.name: The Trail Warms
callingEdges.desc: Cold Trail may be worked twice a day, and a bearing you take once holds for a week without repeating it.

callingEdges.name: No Such Person
callingEdges.desc: Never Was Here reaches a whole county rather than a place, and paper about you goes missing along with the rest.

callingEdges.name: Bench-Tested
callingEdges.desc: Two contraptions may be tuned at once rather than one, and a tuned contraption may be handed to somebody else already tuned.

callingEdges.name: The Whole Deck
callingEdges.desc: Marked Deck reads a whole room rather than one person: one true hidden thing about each of up to four people you can see.

callingEdges.name: The Middle Part
callingEdges.desc: Called shots cost you nothing at all, and you may change your grip, your weapon and your cover in the same Beat.

callingEdges.name: Sworn and Standing
callingEdges.desc: Deputized hands keep their oath for a week rather than a day, and one of them may take a hit meant for you.

callingEdges.name: Kept Count
callingEdges.desc: Winter Count may be called twice a session, and the second telling gives the posse the bonus as well as you.

callingEdges.name: Read the Whole Seam
callingEdges.desc: The Deep Vein reaches five miles rather than one, and names what is down there without your having to guess it first.

callingEdges.name: Two Doses
callingEdges.desc: You carry a second dose, and a patient raised by either may act for twenty minutes rather than ten.

callingEdges.name: The Song Carries
callingEdges.desc: The Long Song may be sung over a whole camp of any size, and those who hear it are proof against fear until the next dusk.

callingEdges.name: The Parish Wide
callingEdges.desc: Your parish includes anyone who has ever taken shelter under your roof, and two of them turn up each session rather than one.

callingEdges.name: The Fire Catches
callingEdges.desc: A camp meeting leaves behind a standing congregation: that town will answer a call from you once, later, however far away you are.

callingEdges.name: The Circle Holds
callingEdges.desc: The Helping Spirits may be sent to every ally at once, and the spirits of a place will answer two questions rather than one.

callingEdges.name: The Third Night
callingEdges.desc: You may keep watch for a week rather than three nights before it tells, and one soul under your watch heals a Lasting Injury over it.

callingEdges.name: The Longer Book
callingEdges.desc: Your book holds twice as many names, and a name in it cannot lie to you in any tongue, at any distance.

callingEdges.name: It Volunteers
callingEdges.desc: Once per session the Patron answers a question you did not ask, at the moment it becomes relevant, whether or not you wanted it.

callingEdges.name: Told Twice
callingEdges.desc: A lie of yours that is disproved may be told again, once, to a different audience, as though it never had been.

callingEdges.name: Interest Deferred
callingEdges.desc: Damage taken through The Deeper Bargain may be pushed onto a willing soul who has agreed to it, once per scene.

callingEdges.name: The Third Beast
callingEdges.desc: A third familiar comes to you and binds. The three of them will not be in the same county, and you will manage.

signs.name: Debt Collected
signs.desc: Name a creature you can see and mark it as owing. Your next blow against it, by hand or gun or Sign, deals an extra 1d6. Backlash: If the mark goes uncollected before the scene ends, you take that 1d6 yourself.

signs.name: The Lender's Ear
signs.desc: Put a question to whatever it is you deal with, framed so that yes or no will answer it. You get the one word. It is accurate. The one word given, the working is done. Backlash: It remembers that you asked, and asking is a thing that accrues.

signs.name: Coin of Pain
signs.desc: The trade run backward: open your own arm and buy 1d6 Nerve with the Blood. Some nights this is the only bank still open. Backlash: Work it twice in a session and the second working costs a Mark as well.

signs.name: Rot the Wound
signs.desc: A wound you dealt this scene will not close. The creature saves or takes 1d6 each round until it is doctored, bound, or dead. Backlash: The next wound dealt to you behaves the same way, and you cannot doctor your own.

signs.name: The Grasping Dark
signs.desc: Shadows within twenty feet take hold. Creatures there save or are held fast until they break loose with a Strength check against your Sign DC. Backlash: The dark does not distinguish. Your companions are standing in it too.

signs.name: The Borrowed Face
signs.desc: Wear the face of someone the dark has already taken. For an hour you are them to any eye, any voice, any old friend who ought to know better. Backlash: For that hour you also remember being them, and some of it stays after the face goes.

signs.name: The Crimson Word
signs.desc: You speak a syllable that was not shaped for a human mouth, and a creature you can see takes 3d6 as its own blood turns against it. Backlash: On a natural 1, or a critical failure to overcome its resistance, you take the damage.

signs.name: The Hungering Hand
signs.desc: Your touch takes 2d6 Blood from a living creature and gives half of it to you. It saves for half, and it feels exactly what it is. Backlash: Take Blood this way three times in a day and you must save or begin to prefer it.

signs.name: Feed the Ledger
signs.desc: Pay in the only coin that never runs short. The next Sign you work this scene costs no Nerve and no Blood, and its dice are maximized. Backlash: None, and that is the trouble with it. The bill is already paid and it is never refunded.

signs.name: The Black Contract
signs.cost: Ten minutes · 4 Nerve and 1 Mark · Will save
signs.desc: Bind a creature that can understand you to a single promise. It saves; on a failure it cannot break the promise, and both of you know the terms exactly. It holds until the promise is kept, or the creature is destroyed. Backlash: You are bound to your half of it on the same terms, and it read the wording more carefully than you did.

signs.name: Open the Vein of the World
signs.cost: 1 Beat · 5 Nerve and 1 Mark · Reflex save
signs.desc: The ground splits along something that was never a fault line. Every creature within thirty feet takes 6d8 and saves for half. The crack does not close. Backlash: The ground remembers. That country gains a step of Taint, permanently.

signs.name: The Calling
signs.desc: You call something out of the dark to bargain or to serve, and it comes. What it is, what it wants, and whether it consents to leave are the Keeper's to decide. It stays until it is sent back, or until it has what it came for. Backlash: The most dangerous Sign in this book. Work it last, or never.

signs.name: Cold Lamp
signs.desc: A light rises off your hand that sheds no warmth and throws no shadow, bright as a good lantern, lasting an hour. It cannot be blown out, drowned, or hidden. Backlash: It cannot be hidden. Everything in that dark now knows exactly where you are standing.

signs.name: Salt & Iron
signs.desc: A handful of blessed salt or cold-iron filings thrown wide. Uncanny things within ten feet save or recoil, and the Marked feel its sting whether they meant to stand in it or not. The salt is thrown and it is done. Backlash: None. This is the kindest Sign in the book, and the weakest.

signs.name: The Listening
signs.desc: Lay your palm flat on a wall, a table, a floorboard, and hear what was spoken in that room within the past day. You get the words. Tone, and who was lying, you must judge yourself. Backlash: You also hear whatever else has been speaking in that room, which is not always a person.

signs.name: Witch-Sight
signs.desc: For a scene you see the unnatural plainly: the Marked, the haunted, the places where the world has worn thin. Distance does not help it and neither does daylight. Backlash: What you are looking at may notice that you are looking.

signs.name: Deadman's Coat
signs.desc: For a scene the eye slides off you the way it slides off a fencepost. You are not invisible; you are uninteresting, which in a crowded room works better. Backlash: Speak, strike, or draw and it breaks at once, and whoever was nearest is startled into looking straight at you.

signs.name: Foul the Working
signs.desc: Someone within sight has begun to work something, and you are on the same wires they are. Grab the line and cross it. Roll d20 + half your level + your Sign ability against their working DC; on a success the working comes apart at once, its price already spent, and nothing happens at all. This answers anything worked, a Sign or a Miracle or the thing a creature does with its mouth, because the dark does not care whose hands are on it. Backlash: on a natural 1 the working lands on you instead, at full strength, and you may foul nothing else this scene.

signs.name: Hollow Step
signs.desc: Step into one shadow and out of another within sight, as far as a stone's throw. You arrive whole, which is not guaranteed and is worth remarking on. The step is taken and it is done. Backlash: Some part of you arrives late: Frightened 1 until your next turn.

signs.name: The Stilling
signs.desc: A word and a gesture. One living creature within sight saves or is held fast, unable to act, for one round per two levels you hold. Backlash: On a failed working you are stilled instead, for the same count.

signs.name: The Tally
signs.desc: Ask the dark one question and receive an answer that is true, partial, and unwelcome. It does not lie. It simply declines to be helpful. The answer given, the working is done. Backlash: The answer costs a Dread Check, and a deep enough truth gains a Mark.

signs.name: Borrowed Breath
signs.desc: Lend a dying companion a measure of your own life. Heal them 2d8 and take half that number in Blood yourself, which does not come back until you rest. Backlash: If they die anyway, you gain +1 Mark. The dark keeps the loan regardless.

signs.name: Nail the Shadow
signs.desc: Drive an iron nail through a creature's shadow. It saves or cannot move from that spot until the nail is pulled, though it may still fight, and will. Backlash: Pull the nail carelessly and the shadow comes with it, attached to you until dawn.

signs.name: The Long Whisper
signs.desc: Speak a sentence into the ear of someone you have met, wherever they are, as though you stood behind them. They may answer once. Most do not, the first time. The way stays open for the scene. Backlash: Anything between you that can hear the dark hears it too, and now has both your names.

signs.name: The Unburdening
signs.desc: Take another soul's terror onto yourself. Clear their Frightened condition and restore 1d6 of their Nerve; you lose that much of your own. Backlash: You take their memory of the thing along with the fear, and it does not fade on the ordinary schedule.

signs.name: The Reckoning Hour
signs.desc: Look at a creature and learn the one thing that will kill it: silver, fire, its own name spoken backward, a blessed round, the fourth cut and not the third. Backlash: It learns the same about you, in the same moment, and it does not have to work a Sign to use what it learns.

signs.name: Unmake the Working
signs.desc: End another's Sign as it is spoken or after it has settled. Roll your Sign DC against theirs; the higher unmakes the lower, and a tie leaves both standing. The unmaking is resolved at once. Backlash: Fail and you have paid the Nerve and announced yourself to a worker who now knows your range.

signs.name: Ward of the Threshold
signs.desc: Chalk, salt, and a spoken name across a doorway. Until dawn nothing uncanny crosses it uninvited, and an invitation once given cannot be taken back that night. Backlash: The ward holds both ways. What is already inside stays inside with you.

signs.name: The Debt Called In
signs.desc: Everything out here owes something to something. Name a creature you can see and call in what it owes, whether or not you are the one it owes it to. It takes 6d6 at once and is Frightened of you until the end of its next turn, and there is no save, because a debt is not an opinion. Backlash: you take a point of Mark for having reached that far into a ledger that was never yours, and that is the whole of the price.

signs.name: The Long Night
signs.desc: Hold a soul at the very edge of death until dawn. They do not worsen, do not wake, and cannot be killed by anything short of fire or the deliberate hand of something old. Backlash: Whatever was coming for them waits at the foot of the bed until sunrise, and it is patient, and it can be seen.

signs.name: Knot the Wind
signs.desc: Tie the weather into a length of cord: three knots, three winds. Loose one later for a gust, a squall, or a good hour of driving rain. Backlash: Loose all three at once and the weather comes as it pleases, over country you had not intended to include.

signs.name: Sour the Milk
signs.desc: The small malice the Craft is famous for. A creature you can see takes a −2 on its very next roll, and the milk goes off, and the bread will not rise. The malice holds until that roll is made. Backlash: None worth the name, which is why every witch in the territories knows it.

signs.name: The Green Hand
signs.desc: Coax what grows into doing you a kindness. Treat a wound for 1d8, or bring a field, a poultice, or a half-dead horse back from the edge of ruin. Backlash: Whatever you healed it with dies, and the ground it stood in stays bare for a season.

signs.name: Cat's Errand
signs.desc: Send your familiar out and ride behind its eyes at any distance, for as long as you sit still and let it work. It can carry a Sign of Rank 1 in its mouth and deliver it. It holds until you rise or are struck, and then you are back behind your own eyes. Backlash: What happens to the familiar out there happens while you are looking through its eyes.

signs.name: Crossing the Threshold
signs.desc: Make a house yours. Nothing uncanny may enter it uninvited while you sleep under its roof, and it will know it is being kept out, and it will mind. The ward holds until dawn, and must be laid again each night you want it. Backlash: You must sleep there. A witch who wards a house and rides away has built a very good box for someone else.

signs.name: The Nail and the Name
signs.desc: You have had the name, or the hair, or a drop of them, since long before tonight. Drive the nail into anything wooden and say it. The creature saves at once or takes 2d6 and is Slowed for a round; on a success it takes half and keeps its feet. You need its true name, something of its body, or a thing it touched and left, and hearing a name shouted across a room in the middle of a fight counts. This is the Craft doing in one Beat what it spent a week getting ready to do. Backlash: the nail is spent whether or not the working lands, and so is whatever you had of them.

signs.name: The Poppet
signs.desc: Bind a doll to a person whose hair, blood, or name you hold. What you do to the doll, they feel, up to 2d6 and a save to halve it, at any distance you can imagine. Backlash: Whoever holds the poppet holds the working, and dolls are small and easily pocketed.

signs.name: The Brewing
signs.desc: Cook a Sign of Rank 2 or lower down into a draught and cork it. It keeps a month and works for whoever drinks it, which need not be you. Backlash: It works for whoever drinks it. Label the bottle.

signs.name: The Ninefold Knot
signs.desc: Nine knots in a red cord and a name said over each. A creature saves or cannot work its own uncanny power for nine days, though it may fight, flee, and remember you fine. Backlash: Cut the cord early and the nine days come back all at once, on you.

signs.name: Ask the Line
signs.desc: Call up a woman of your own crooked line, dead these many years, and ask her. She answers plainly, at length, and with opinions about your choices. She stays for the scene. Backlash: She may decline to go back, and a dead grandmother in the house is a long and particular haunting.

signs.name: The Turning
signs.desc: The evil eye put to the one use that is not spite. As a blow or a working comes at you, look at what sent it. It saves or the harm goes back the way it came at once, all of it, and the sender takes what it meant for you. On a success it lands as intended and you have spent the Nerve for a hard look. Backlash: everyone who sees you do this remembers your face, and no witch has ever had a good week afterward.

signs.name: The Widow's Curse
signs.desc: The old curse, laid properly and meant. A person saves or carries a lasting misfortune of your naming until the wrong you cursed them for is put right. Backlash: It cannot be lifted by you, or by anyone, until that wrong is actually put right. Curse carefully, and be sure of the wrong.

signs.name: The Hearth Unbroken
signs.desc: For one night a place is genuinely safe. Nothing uncanny crosses, no Dread Check is called, and every soul under that roof wakes with full Nerve and Blood. Backlash: One night only, and the same roof will not answer twice in the same season. Choose the night with care.

signs.name: The Old Woman's Bargain
signs.desc: Trade a year of your own life for a working of any Rank you know, at no other cost, worked as though you were the greatest of your line. The year is taken from the far end. The bargain is struck at once, and what you bought is worked as any other. Backlash: None at the time. The Craft always collects at the far end, and it is never late.

signs.name: The Unwritten Hour
signs.desc: Say that the last round did not happen, and it did not. Everything since your own last turn comes undone: the shot, the fall, the word spoken, the door opened. Everyone acts again from where they stood, knowing nothing. Backlash: you remember both hours, and for a day you cannot reliably tell which of the two you are living in. Roll a flat check the first time it matters, and the Keeper will not tell you why.

signs.name: Nothing Answers Here
signs.desc: Draw the line and close it. For an hour, inside a hundred feet of where you drew it, no Sign works, no Miracle is granted, no uncanny thing does the thing it does, and nothing may be summoned, banished, healed by grace or harmed by a working. It is quiet in there in a way that frightens people who have never heard it. Backlash: you are inside it too, and you cannot lift it early.

signs.name: The Long Winter
signs.desc: Lay cold on a country and let it stay. For a season, the valley or the town you name is colder than it should be: crops fail slowly, the sick get sicker, the roads close early, and anything that was buried stays buried. The old women who can do this rarely explain why they have. Backlash: you feel the cold yourself for the whole of it, and no fire ever quite reaches you again.

signs.name: What Was Promised
signs.desc: Something out there owes you, and you have decided to say so out loud. Name the debt, and you take payment instantly: any single effect of a Sign of Rank 5 or under, worked instantly and without its own cost, whether or not you know it. Backlash: the ledger is not yours to read. Whatever you took is added to what you owe at twice the value, and the Keeper decides when that is collected and from whom.

signs.name: The Ground Gives
signs.desc: The country stops holding still. For the scene, within sight, you move the ground: a road becomes a ravine, a river runs the other way, a wall is somewhere else, a floor opens, a hill stands where there was flat. One change a round, each of them real and each of them permanent unless something changes it back. Backlash: the ground remembers who moved it, and every working you attempt on that land afterward costs one more Nerve, for good.

signs.name: No One Sleeps Tonight
signs.desc: Take the night off a place. For a full night, nobody inside a mile sleeps, rests, recovers Blood or Nerve, regains a pool, or heals by any means short of a Miracle. The uncanny do not restore themselves either, which is generally the point, and the living get to dawn with nothing left. Backlash: you do not sleep for three nights afterward, and the third one is bad.

signs.name: The Turning of the Year
signs.desc: Put years into a thing or take them out, permanently. A door rots off its hinges; a corpse is bones; a green field is a harvest; a wound is an old scar; a young man is old. A creature resists with a Fortitude save against your Sign DC, and a willing one need not. Ten years is the usual reach, and forty is the most anyone has managed. Backlash: the years have to go somewhere. They go into you, and they show.

signs.name: Sell the Night
signs.desc: Offer up a night that has not happened yet. Name a night in the coming year and hand it over; until then you work every Sign at one Rank higher than you have earned, pay one less Nerve for each, and cannot be reduced below 1 Blood by anything uncanny. Backlash: on the night you sold, you are not yours. Where you went and what was done with you is the Keeper's, and you will hear about some of it later.

signs.name: The Word Under the Word
signs.cost: One minute · your whole pool of Nerve and 1 Mark, permanently
signs.desc: Every working has a word under it that nobody says. Say it. One working of any kind, anywhere you have ever been — a curse, a ward, a binding, a Miracle, a Sign, a thing a creature was made to do — comes apart and has never worked. It may be one that finished a hundred years ago, and the hundred years rearrange themselves around its absence. Backlash: your Mark rises by one and does not come down, and one working of your own, chosen by the Keeper, comes apart at the same moment.

signs.name: The House That Stands
signs.cost: One night · your whole pool of Nerve, permanently
signs.desc: Over a night's work you make a place yours in a way that outlasts you. Nothing uncanny enters it uninvited, ever. Nothing inside it can be scried, called, compelled or taken. It does not burn, and the weather leaves it alone, and it will be standing when the town around it is a scatter of foundations. Backlash: you may never have another, you may not leave it for more than a season without it beginning to fail, and something will spend the rest of your life on the porch waiting to be asked in.

signs.name: The Name You Were Given
signs.cost: One minute · your whole pool of Nerve and 2 Mark, permanently
signs.desc: Everything that was made was named when it was made, and the name is still true. Speak the true name of one creature you can see, however old and however great, and it must do one thing you say, in one sentence, at once and completely, whatever it is. It cannot refuse and there is no save. Backlash: it now knows that you know, it knows yours, and it has as long as it likes to do something about that. Very few workers have used this twice, and the ones who did were not around to be asked why.

miracles.name: A Light Unfailing
miracles.desc: A steady light rises at your word, warm where Cold Lamp is cold, and lasts an hour. The uncanny will not willingly step into it, and the Marked find it hard to meet.

miracles.name: The Steadying Word
miracles.desc: Speak to one soul who can hear you and mean it. They shake off Frightened, or gain +2 on their next save against fear. It works on the faithless and the profane alike; steadiness is not particular about who receives it. The steadiness holds until that save is rolled.

miracles.name: Hands Clasped
miracles.desc: Take an ally's hand, or bid them take another's. For the scene the two of you share your saves against fear — whichever of you rolls better, both use — and neither may be made to flee while the other stands.

miracles.name: Not While I Stand
miracles.desc: Something uncanny is being worked where you can see it. Say no. Roll d20 + half your level + your Miracle ability against the worker's DC; on a success it comes apart at once, its price already spent. You may answer a Sign, a curse in the moment it lands, or the working of any uncanny thing. You may not answer a Miracle: what is asked for in good faith is not yours to refuse. Nothing here can turn on you and no failure is worse than failing, so you may do it as often as you can pay for it.

miracles.name: The Blessing of the Road
miracles.desc: Bless a journey before it is begun. For the next day the party ignores the first hazard of the trail and travels at +2 on Survival to find the way, the water, and the safe camp.

miracles.name: Anoint the Iron
miracles.desc: Touch a weapon, speak over it, and give it back. For the scene it counts as blessed and as silver both, and every hit it lands on something uncanny deals an extra 1d6. It does not have to be your weapon and it does not have to stay in your hands; put it in the hands of whoever out here is best with it, which is rarely you.

miracles.name: The Unclean Named
miracles.desc: Point and name a thing for what it truly is. It saves or its nature stands revealed to all who can hear you, and it suffers a −2 against you and yours until the scene ends. Some things have not been named aloud in a long age, and do not care for it.

miracles.name: The Warding Psalm
miracles.desc: As an uncanny blow lands on you or a soul beside you, speak the psalm and turn it: the attack is halved, and its wielder gives ground a step. You may do this once per round, and not on ordinary lead.

miracles.name: Rebuke the Dark
miracles.desc: Raise your voice against the unclean things in sight. Each lesser uncanny saves or flees you for a round per two levels, and a greater one that fails is Frightened and gives ground. The oldest of them only smile — but the small ones run.

miracles.name: The Vigil
miracles.desc: Keep the watch and pray it through. Until dawn, no one in the camp may be surprised or driven by fear, and every soul but you sleeps easy under it. You take no rest, and you will feel the want of it come morning.

miracles.name: The Covenant
miracles.desc: Spread your arms and stand for them. For the scene, no ally who can hear you may be brought below 1 Blood by uncanny harm — struck to the edge of death, and no further, while your voice holds. Ordinary lead still kills as it pleases. The dark does not get to.

miracles.name: The Hour Is Not Yours
miracles.desc: When a soul you can see is about to die, and die rather than merely fall, say aloud that the hour is not yours to take. It is not taken. They lie Dying one point above dead and no worse, stable at once and until somebody reaches them. Whatever was coming for that soul now knows your name, knows you said it out loud, and has been given a reason to learn where you sleep.

miracles.name: The Miracle Plain
miracles.desc: Once, and never lightly: ask for the thing that cannot be asked for, and now and again receive it. Undo one calamity of the moment just past — a death, a fire caught, a fall — as the Keeper allows. It empties your whole pool to nothing and cannot be tried again until you have rested and given thanks. Most prayers are not answered. This is about the ones that are.

miracles.name: Salt the Threshold
miracles.desc: Lay a line of blessed salt across a door, a window, a circle of camp. Uncanny things save or cannot cross it until dawn or until the line is broken by a living hand — theirs cannot break it.

miracles.name: The Litany of Weakness
miracles.desc: Recite what you know of a thing's banes — the silver, the fire, the true name, the running water. Your next Judgment against it deals +1d8, the knowledge sharpening the blow.

miracles.name: Silver the Round
miracles.desc: Bless and silver-wash a handful of ammunition on the spot. The next three shots fired from it count as silver and blessed for overcoming the uncanny's resistances, whoever pulls the trigger. The blessing holds until those three shots are fired, or until dawn, whichever comes first.

miracles.name: The Branding
miracles.desc: Mark your quarry with the sign of the hunt. For a day you always know its direction and rough distance, it cannot hide from you by any uncanny means, and it knows, wherever it runs, that it has been marked.

miracles.name: Consecrate the Killing Ground
miracles.desc: Sanctify a patch of ground and make it a trap for the unclean. Within it, uncanny things fight at −2 and cannot flee by any supernatural means — no stepping through shadow, no sinking into earth. What comes onto this ground leaves it on your terms or not at all.

miracles.name: The Reckoning Fire
miracles.desc: Call a consecrated flame that burns the unclean and spares the rest. Every uncanny thing in a wide reach takes 6d6 holy fire, save for half, and what the fire kills does not rise, reform, or return. The living may stand in it unharmed. The dark has no such luck.

miracles.name: Asperges Me
miracles.desc: Sprinkle holy water and speak the old antiphon. Each Marked or uncanny thing within reach saves or takes 1d6 and recoils, hissing at the water and the Latin both.

miracles.name: The Sign of the Cross
miracles.desc: The oldest gesture in the Church, made in earnest. You or an ally beside you gains +2 against the next uncanny working or fear effect — if the hand is quick enough to make it in time. The blessing holds until it is spent.

miracles.name: The Litany of the Saints
miracles.desc: Call the long roll of the faithful dead, and let the living hear how many stood before them. Every ally who listens gains one reroll against fear, kept until the scene ends or it is spent.

miracles.name: Extreme Unction
miracles.desc: Anoint the dying with oil and the last words. They are stabilized at once, wake with 1d6 Blood, and — whatever comes after — cannot rise as one of the restless dead. The rite is a mercy first and a precaution second, but it is both.

miracles.name: The Interdict
miracles.desc: Lay the Church's ban upon a place, an object, or a grave. For a day and a night no uncanny thing may enter it, use it, or draw strength from it, as though the ground itself had been forbidden to them by an authority older than their hunger.

miracles.name: Te Deum
miracles.desc: The great hymn of thanksgiving, sung as a weapon. A lesser uncanny thing is banished outright; a greater one saves or is Frightened and Slowed the whole scene; and every soul who kneels and sings with you is eased of the Mark's symptoms for a day. Two thousand years are in the words.

miracles.name: Set the Bone
miracles.desc: Splint, wrap, and set what is broken. Ease the penalty of one Lasting Injury for a day, buying a wounded soul the working hours the country would sooner deny them.

miracles.name: The Poultice
miracles.desc: Press a prepared remedy to the hurt. It heals 1d8 over the next few minutes and costs only the one point — the small, sure mending you lean on so the deep well stays full for worse.

miracles.name: The Fever Broken
miracles.desc: Sit the long watch and break the fever. End the next worsening of a disease or poison and grant a fresh save against it at +4. Most of doctoring is refusing to let a thing get worse. The watch is kept and the working is done.

miracles.name: The Sleep of Healing
miracles.desc: Sing a hurt soul down into a true healing sleep. They recover double from tonight's rest and wake clear of fear and easy of mind, which in this country is the rarer of the two cures. The sleep holds until dawn.

miracles.name: The Life Shared
miracles.desc: Open the well to more than one at once. Divide your healing among every ally you can reach — 2d8 to be shared out as you choose — the mercy spread thin across many rather than poured into one.

miracles.name: The Long Mercy
miracles.desc: Hold a mortally hurt soul back from the door for a full day and night without the well draining further, so that a true cure, a hard ride, or a better healer may reach them in time. You cannot mend what took them. You can refuse to let it finish the work today.

miracles.name: Call to the Mourner's Bench
miracles.desc: Round on one sinner — mortal or monstrous — and call them forward to answer for it. They save or lose their next action, rooted and named before the whole room.

miracles.name: The Amen Corner
miracles.desc: Work the crowd, and let them work back. Allies who can hear you and answer aloud gain +1 to hit for a round. Faith, the Preacher will tell you, is a call and a response.

miracles.name: The Altar Call
miracles.desc: Lay hands and call a soul back to itself: heal a touched ally 2d6, and they may at once reroll one save they have just failed. Come forward, the Preacher says. It is not too late — not quite yet.

miracles.name: Testify
miracles.desc: Speak a true and terrible thing into the silence. One creature saves or is Frightened 2 and made to blurt the last lie it told. The Preacher has found that the guilty fear the truth far worse than the gun. The naming is resolved at once; the fear it leaves lessens a step each turn, as fear does.

miracles.name: The Camp Meeting
miracles.desc: Preach a rolling revival and do not stop. For three rounds, so long as you keep the Word going and take no other action, every ally who can hear you regains Nerve and shakes one condition at the start of each round. The tent shakes. So does the dark outside it.

miracles.name: Pentecost
miracles.desc: Tongues of fire, and every ear hearing in its own language. For the scene your Brimstone strikes every uncanny thing you can see at once, and the Marked cannot resist it by their Mark. The fire does not fall often. When it does, it does not ask permission.

miracles.name: A Word to the Small Spirits
miracles.desc: Ask the little spirits of a place one plain thing, courteously: where the water lies, who passed this way, what waits in the next draw. They answer plainly, if they answer, and remember that you asked kindly. The answer given, the working is done.

miracles.name: The Offering
miracles.desc: Leave tobacco, salt, or bread, and name the debt. The spirits of that ground grant safe passage, or +2 on one task done there, for as long as the gift is respected and the ground not fouled.

miracles.name: Borrow the Beast's Gift
miracles.desc: Ask a nearby animal spirit for the loan of one gift, and wear it for a scene: an owl's eyes in the dark, a wolf's nose, a hare's speed, a bear's thick hide. The spirits lend gladly and expect the courtesy of thanks.

miracles.name: Set the Pack On
miracles.desc: Call whatever hunts this country and point. For one round the creature you named is beset by things that are almost not there: it stands Off-Guard, takes 2d6 at once, and cannot take the Aim. The spirits do not stay, and they will not come twice in one night for the same asking, so choose the moment rather than the enemy.

miracles.name: Turn the Weather
miracles.desc: Coax the sky a step kinder or crueler for the hour — a fog to cover a retreat, a break in the rain, a wind at your back or in the enemy's face. The weather keeps its own counsel and grants the favor, not the command.

miracles.name: The Spirit-Snare
miracles.desc: Draw the knot that holds a spirit or a restless dead thing fast. It saves or cannot leave the spot until dawn or until you loose it — able to speak, and to rage, and to bargain, but not to go.

miracles.name: Call the Great Spirit
miracles.desc: Call a great spirit of storm, of beast, or of the honored dead, and it answers for a scene, lending its power to your hand without the peril of wearing its mask. It comes as a neighbor answers a knock — because you have kept faith, and because you asked.

miracles.name: Hand Held
miracles.desc: Take hold of a soul who has just failed a Dread Check and give them something to hold back. They reroll it at once, and keep the second result even if it is worse. Most take the second result gladly. The ones who do not are why you keep hold a moment longer than they want.

miracles.name: The Watch Kept
miracles.desc: Walk the bounds of a camp, a room, a cellar stair, naming what you mean to keep out. Until you sleep or leave, every soul inside takes +2 on Dread Checks, and nothing uncanny crosses the line you walked without you knowing the moment it does. It does not stop anything. It only means you are never the last to find out.

miracles.name: The Lamp Unquenched
miracles.desc: A flame you have lit cannot be put out for the rest of the scene: not by wind, water, smothering, or anything that walks. Its light does not carry further than a lamp's, and that is the whole of the comfort, but nothing that hates the light can approach within its circle without spending its whole turn to do it.

miracles.name: Nothing Comes In
miracles.desc: Stand in a doorway, a gate, a stair-head, and refuse it. For a scene, anything uncanny that would cross must first make a Will save against your Miracle DC; on a failure it cannot cross at all this round and must spend its turn trying again. It can still reach through. It can still call. It cannot simply walk in, and a great many of them have never had to learn what to do about that.

miracles.name: The Body Kept Whole
miracles.desc: Sit the night with a corpse and keep it. It will not rise, it cannot be raised, called, worn, or spoken through, and nothing may take from it what it carried in life. This holds until the body is buried or burned, and it holds against the thing that made it as surely as against any other. It is the oldest work your order does and the one nobody thanks you for.

miracles.name: She Will Not Be Moved
miracles.desc: For one scene you cannot be moved from where you stand: not shoved, dragged, teleported, banished, swallowed, possessed, charmed, or persuaded. You may still choose to walk, and choosing is the only thing that moves you. One soul you have hold of shares it while you keep hold. What this costs is that you are also standing exactly where everything can find you, for a whole scene, on purpose.

miracles.name: The Cup Not Emptied
miracles.desc: Bless what little there is. Food, water, medicine, powder, lamp oil, bandage — whatever is in front of you, there is now enough of it for everyone here, for a week. It is plain and it is sufficient and it does not keep past the week. A great many hard winters have turned on somebody being able to do this.

miracles.name: The Requiem
miracles.desc: Sing the whole of it over a burying ground, a battlefield, a burned house, a mine. Every restless dead thing in that place is laid to rest at once and cannot be raised from it again by any means. Those who can be told what happened to them are told. Those who cannot are simply let go, which is most of them.

miracles.name: The Whole Town Rises
miracles.desc: Preach until the place stands up. Every living soul within earshot who is not hostile to you recovers all Blood and Nerve, shakes every condition, and for the next hour will fight, carry, dig or stand where you ask them to. They will not do anything they believe is wrong, and afterward they will be very tired and will want to know what came over them.

miracles.name: The Body Made Whole
miracles.desc: Put a person back the way they were made. All Blood restored, every disease, poison and Affliction gone, every Lasting Injury undone, limbs and sight and hearing returned. Whatever was done to them is not done to them any more. It works once on any one soul, ever, and both of you will know afterward which day it was.

miracles.name: Out of the Depths
miracles.desc: Reach for somebody who has been taken. Name a soul who is possessed, bound, called away, hollowed out, sold, or being worn by something else, and pull. They come back at once, out of whatever has them, whole enough to speak and to say what happened. Whatever had them is now aware that you can do this, and where you were standing when you did it.

miracles.name: The Council of the Dead
miracles.desc: Call the dead of a place together and sit down with them. Every spirit within a mile that will come, comes, and they answer honestly for an hour: what was done here, by whom, where it is now, and what would settle it. They are not obliged to be kind and they are frequently not. Once in a while one of them asks you for something, and then you have a second problem.

miracles.name: The Ground Made Holy
miracles.desc: Consecrate ground and mean it permanently. Nothing uncanny may enter, use, or draw strength from the bounded place ever again; the Marked feel the boundary from outside; the dead buried in it stay buried and quiet. It ends only if the ground is broken deliberately by a living hand, which somebody will eventually get around to.

miracles.name: Until Morning
miracles.desc: Sit down with them and say that this is not the night. Until dawn, no soul inside the room, the camp or the house may die: the dying do not go, the mortal wound waits, the sickness holds where it is. It does not cure any of it and morning still comes. What it buys is the hours, and the hours are usually what was wanted.

miracles.name: The Answer
miracles.cost: One minute · your whole pool of Faith
miracles.desc: Most prayers are not answered. Ask, once, for a single thing, in your own words, aloud, in front of whoever is there — and it is granted, whatever it was. The dead one back. The fire out. The army turned. The sickness lifted off a county. The thing that has been coming, not coming. There is no save, no roll and no limit but the one thing. Afterward your pool is empty until you have rested and given thanks, and you will spend the rest of your life being careful about what you ask for, having found out that it works.

miracles.name: Greater Love
miracles.cost: Reaction · your whole pool of Faith
miracles.desc: Step in front of all of it. Any harm, effect, death, taking or unmaking about to fall on any number of souls you can see falls on you instead, entire and undivided, and they are untouched and unaware until it is over. You will very likely not survive it. If you do not, you cannot be raised, called back, or spoken to afterward by any means: you are where the people you saved are not, and that was the arrangement.

miracles.name: The Long Road Home
miracles.cost: One hour · your whole pool of Faith
miracles.desc: Take everyone home. Every soul who has been with you and is willing, living or freshly dead or lost or held somewhere else, is brought at once to one place you name that any of you has ever called home, safely, together, however far it is and whatever holds them. Doors open. Distances shorten. The dead walk in with the rest. It costs you the road: you may not use this again, and you will never afterward be able to travel anywhere the ordinary way without knowing exactly how much shorter it could have been.

weapons.name: Fists / Boots
weapons.traits: Nonlethal unless you mean it, Agile

weapons.name: Knife / Bowie
weapons.traits: Concealable, Agile, +1 on a Sudden Strike

armor.name: Heavy Duster / Coat
armor.note: Nothing, and it keeps the cold out

armor.name: Scavenged Iron Plate
armor.note: –2 Speed, and loud with it; alone of the three it stops a pistol ball

callings.name: Bounty Hunter
callings.blurb: Some come to the frontier to take what others carried; the Bounty Hunter comes for the men who took it.

perk.name: Paper on Him
perk.desc: Give you a night in any town with a jail, a telegraph office, or a saloon, and you will come back knowing who wants a man, what for, how much, and whether the paper is still good. You will also come back knowing who wants you, which is worth finding out early.

fight.brings: The hardest single hit in the book, when you set it up. Bushwhack turns a foe who has not seen you yet into four extra dice by 10th level.
fight.costs: A d8, and dice that only come when you have the drop. A fight you walk into face-first is a fight you have with a gun and nothing else.

featureDescs.Bushwhack: Bringing a man in is not a fair fight, and you do not pretend otherwise. Once per turn, when you Strike a quarry who is unaware of you, who has not yet acted in the fight, or whom an ally threatens, deal the listed extra damage. The ambush is the whole of the art — a bounty man forced to trade blows in the open with a cornered killer has already made his mistake.
featureDescs.Quick Hands: Years of needing your iron — or your irons, the manacle kind — a half-second sooner than the other man. You draw, holster, reload, or snap on a cuff as part of another action rather than spending a Beat on it, and add +2 to the roll that decides who acts first. Lockpicks, knots, and a fugitive's hidden pockets answer to these hands as readily as a trigger does.
featureDescs.Road Sense: You have laid enough ambushes to know when you are walking into one. Gain +2 on Notice against traps, tails, and lying-in-wait, and you are never caught flat — you act in the first round of a fight even when surprise is called against you. The hunted set snares too.
featureDescs.The Drop: With a quarry dead to rights — your iron drawn, his not — you may Demoralize as a single Beat, and a man who yields comes along quiet, hands where you can see them. Against one who calls the bluff, your first Strike counts him as unaware. Dead or alive is his choosing; you are paid the same either way.
featureDescs.Getaway: The catch is only half done until you and your man are clear of his friends. Immediately after you Strike, take a prisoner, or break free, you may Step and then Stride for free; mounted, you may instead vault to the saddle and ride, prisoner and all.
featureDescs.Hard Ride: You and your horse have run down more men — and outrun more of their kin — than you can count. Your mounted Speed increases by 10 feet, you cross rough country a fleeing man must slow for, and once per scene you may close on a single quarry who thought he had lost you, or shake a pursuit of your own, given a moment's lead and a place to turn.
featureDescs.Dead or Alive: At 10th level your name is worth nearly as much as the paper you carry. Once per scene, a Bushwhack you land against an unready quarry is an automatic critical hit. And you are never truly cornered: declare a bolt-hole — a relay horse, a confederate, a lawman who owes you, a back trail only you know — and the Keeper will honor it, once, when all seems lost. A great many men have been promised to the rope, and you are the one who delivers them.
featureDescs.Cold Trail: A trail stops going cold on you. Given a name and one thing that belonged to the man — a hat, a letter, a horse he rode — you may sit an hour with it at dusk and learn the direction he lies in and roughly how far, once each day. It tells you nothing of what stands between. Many a bounty man has ridden four hundred miles on a true bearing and arrived a week after the funeral.
featureDescs.Nowhere to Run: You have closed too many doors to leave one open now. A quarry you have Struck this scene cannot Disengage from you without first beating your Notice with an Athletics or Stealth check, and any cover he takes is cover you have already used yourself. When he runs anyway, your first shot after him counts him unaware.
featureDescs.The Warrant: Your name has become a kind of law. Once per session you may write a warrant of your own — on the back of a bill, on a barn door, on nothing at all — naming one creature or one man. Until the session ends, or the warrant is served, you always know the direction of the named and how far off it lies, your Bushwhack against it is an automatic critical hit, and any lawman, hand or honest citizen who hears the name will help you against it or stand out of your way. Serve it, and the country pays: the Keeper grants one lasting boon out of what the warrant was worth, and the paper goes on the wall of some office where men will read the name for fifty years. Write the wrong name and you will find that out the same way.

options.name: The Stalker
options.boon: You read a quarry's trail and habits and strike from where he never looks; your Bushwhack deals extra dice against a foe who has not yet acted. Mastery (10th): once per scene, a perfect ambush against an unready quarry is an automatic critical that may end the chase before it starts.

options.name: The Posse Boss
options.boon: You ride at the head of a hunting party, swear in hands to the chase, and may Demoralize a whole group at once. Mastery (10th): once per scene, your name alone breaks lesser fugitives who know it — they scatter, surrender, or freeze.

options.name: The Trailsman
options.boon: You handle and run down mounts with ease, and ride harder than any man you hunt. Mastery (10th): once per scene, you run a quarry to ground that no horse and no head start could have saved.

callings.name: Drifter
callings.blurb: The Drifter belongs to no town and answers to no brand. Scout, tracker, horse-thief, bounty-man, or simply a soul who cannot stop moving — the Drifter survives by seeing first, striking once, and being elsewhere by dawn.

perk.name: No Name Sticks
perk.desc: You have used a dozen names and answered to all of them. What you did in one town follows you to the next only if a living soul carries it there on purpose, and every description of you is wrong in at least one particular that matters.

fight.brings: Position. Sudden Strike pays whenever somebody else has the foe's attention, and Evasion means the blast that catches the posse often does not catch you.
fight.costs: Steady attack, a d8, and no answer at all to a thing that has already seen you and is walking straight at you.

featureDescs.Sudden Strike: When you strike a foe who is unaware of you, or whom an ally is engaging (an Off-Guard target; see Conditions), you deal extra damage as shown — the patient violence of the ambush. The dice rise as you advance.
featureDescs.Pathfinder: You move at full speed through wilderness others must crawl through, leave a trail only the gifted can follow, and add your level to checks to track, forage, or find the way.
featureDescs.Ghost / Uncanny Step / Vanish: You learn to disappear. Ghost lets you hide even while briefly observed. Uncanny Step leaves no track on any surface. Vanish lets you drop from sight once per scene, as if the land itself closed over you — out here, perhaps it has.
featureDescs.Evasion: Your reflexes are inhuman. On a successful Reflex save against an effect that would harm an area — a blast, a cave-in, a sweep of fire — you take no harm at all rather than half. On a critical success, you also end your move in any open square adjacent to the danger.
featureDescs.Never Was Here: You have got so good at leaving that the leaving takes the arriving with it. After a night in a place you may spend an hour undoing your own presence in it: the ledger entry, the stall in the livery, the face behind the bar. Anyone questioned about you afterward remembers a man, remembers nothing useful, and grows less certain the harder they are pressed. Dogs and children are unaffected, and neither are the dead.
featureDescs.The Long Odds: Evasion becomes something worse for whatever is throwing at you. On a failed save against an effect Evasion would have halved, you take half instead of full; on a success you take none and may Step for free. The blast that catches the posse has caught you three hundred times, and you have gone under it three hundred times.
featureDescs.Gone: There is no situation you cannot walk out of. Once per session, as a free action at any moment including one in which you are held, bound, buried, grappled, surrounded, unconscious or falling, you are simply elsewhere: any place you could plausibly have reached on foot within the last hour, unharmed, with whatever you were carrying and one thing or one willing soul you had a hand on. Nothing that was watching can say how. The cost is that you leave: whatever you were in the middle of goes on without you, and the country between you and it is a day's ride wide by the time you think better of it.

options.name: The Ghost Trail
options.boon: Gain a bonus to Sneak and Hide, and you may Hide in cover even while observed. Mastery (10th): once per scene, become wholly unseen for a round, striking from nowhere.

options.name: The Hard Trail
options.boon: Ignore the toll of harsh country, weather, and want; +2 Fortitude against the elements. Mastery (10th): once per scene, shrug off the first wound or affliction that would lay you low.

options.name: The Hunter's Trail
options.boon: You never lose a trail and gain +2 against ambush and to read a quarry. Mastery (10th): once per scene, study a foe a moment and learn the weakness that undoes it.

callings.name: Engineer
callings.blurb: Everyone else out here is trying to survive the country. You are trying to make it hold still long enough to build something on.

perk.name: Every Machine Answers
perk.desc: A quarter hour with any built thing and you can say what it does, what is wrong with it, and what putting it right would take: a lock, a pump, a press, a rifle action, a stamp mill, a clock. Whether you can fix it today depends on what is in the wagon. Whether you understand it depends on nothing at all.

fight.brings: Whatever the posse is short of. A frame is a gun, a wall, a hook or a wrench, and every one of them works in somebody else's hands as well as it works in yours.
fight.costs: Steady attack, a d8, and a Beat and a point of Ingenuity each time. Your best round is the one that makes three other people's rounds better, which is a hard thing to feel proud of while it is happening.

featureDescs.The Contraption: You have built one thing that exists nowhere else. Choose a frame from the list below; you build another at 5th, 8th, 10th and 11th level, and you may rebuild any of them over a night with your tools. Working a frame costs 1 Ingenuity and a Beat, and here is the part that matters: anybody you have shown it to may work it instead of you. On a natural 1, or any time the Keeper rules you have asked too much of it, it breaks; mending it takes an hour and your hands, and it is never quite the same afterward. You have stopped expecting it to be.
featureDescs.A Contraption's Frames: The Repeater. A gun fed by a clock spring and a drum. It Strikes at your attack for 1d10 and never wants reloading. Wind it for a Beat and it fires once on its own at the end of each of your turns until the spring runs down, which takes three rounds. The Bulwark. A folding plate on a tripod that sets in a Beat and gives hard cover to two souls behind it. It weighs what you would expect. Dragging it forward costs somebody a Beat, and somebody always volunteers once the shooting starts. The Winch. A hooked line on a geared drum. Spend a Beat to take hold of one creature within 30 feet: Fortitude (DC 10 + half your level + WIT) or be dragged 10 feet toward you and left Prone. Things with claws in the ground resist it. Things in the air do not. The Governor. A brass regulator that clamps onto any working mechanism and persuades it to stop: a lock, a pump, a rifle action, a jaw that opens on a hinge. It seizes for a round. Against a made thing that fights, a round is a great deal. The Alarum. Wire, a bell and a spring, set across the approaches. Nothing crosses your camp unannounced, and you sleep like a man who has been paid. The Listening Horn. A wall stops being a wall. Set the bell against it and hear what is said on the other side, at a distance the speaker would never credit. The Diving Lamp. Burns wet, burns under, burns in the bad air at the bottom of a shaft, and does not go out because something in the dark would prefer it did. The Heliograph. Mirrors and a shutter on a folding stand. In daylight you can hold a conversation with somebody a mile off, and so can anybody who knows the code, which is the part worth thinking about.
featureDescs.Powder & Fuse: Blasting is a trade and you served it. You cut, time and place a charge without the Keeper calling for a check, and you know to the yard how far back is far enough. Each dawn you prepare two charges of your own, and any prepared explosive you set yourself deals an extra die of its damage.
featureDescs.Jury-Rig: Once per scene, put something back into service with wire, a strap, and language nobody should hear. A broken tool, a jammed action, a snapped trace, a door off its hinge: it works for the rest of the scene, and afterward it is broken again and rather worse.
featureDescs.Cut the Charge: You know what a blast wants to do and where it will go. You take half damage from any explosion, and so does any ally you had a moment to shout at. The shout is required. More of this trade is shouting than the recruiting posters admit.
featureDescs.Field Expedient: Given ten minutes, a few hands and whatever the ground offers, you throw up a work: a barricade, a footbridge, a sluice, a firing step, a hoist. It is ugly, it holds for the scene, and it changes what the ground is worth.
featureDescs.Overbuilt: You have stopped building things that fail when it matters. Your contraptions and field works no longer break on a natural 1, and break at all only when the Keeper rules something genuinely beyond their design was asked of them.
featureDescs.The Machine Age: At 10th level the things you make outlast the making of them. Choose one of your contraptions: it costs no Ingenuity to work, it does not break, and it can be handed to somebody else and will work for them. You have crossed the line between a trick and a tool, and the century coming will be built out of what is on your side of it.
featureDescs.Proving Ground: You have finally got somewhere to test things before they are needed. Given a day and a place to work, you may rebuild any contraption into any other frame, and once per scene you may declare that a contraption you are working has been tuned for exactly this: it does not break on a natural 1, and its save DC rises by 2 against the specific thing you built the tuning for. You were up all night. It shows in the work and it shows in your face.
featureDescs.The Standing Work: Given four hours, a place and hands to help, you raise something that does not travel: a redoubt, a sluice, a spanned gap, a wall with a gate in it. It gives cover the Keeper rates as greater, holds against anything you can still shoot for a scene, and can be worked by anyone you have shown it to. It stays where you built it after you have gone, which is more than most men manage.
featureDescs.The Century Coming: Once per session, you build a thing that does not exist yet. Name the problem in front of the posse and describe the machine that answers it; if the Keeper can imagine it built out of what this century has — iron, steam, powder, wire, glass, water and time — then you have built it, over an hour and whatever it costs, and it works once, fully, at the scale the problem needs. A rail car that outruns a thing on the track behind it. A cage that will hold what nothing holds. A light that reaches the far side of the valley. Afterward it is scrap, and you are the only one who knows how it went together, which is a heavy thing to be.

options.name: The Powderman
options.boon: Charges answer to you. Any explosive you prepare may be shaped: choose which side of it is dangerous, and allies outside that arc take nothing at all. Mastery (10th): once per scene, bring down a structure, a span or a shaft exactly as you intend, in the direction you intend.

options.name: The Machinist
options.boon: Given a day and a workshop you permanently improve one weapon or tool: an extra shot before reloading, one step less Kickback, a jam that clears itself. Only one item at a time carries your work. Mastery (10th): once per scene, one of your contraptions acts on its own for a round, taking a Beat's action you name.

options.name: The Bridgewright
options.boon: Spans, shafts and crossings. You and anyone following you ignore difficult ground and broken country, and a gap that stops a party stops you for ten minutes. Mastery (10th): once per session, build in a day what should have taken a crew a week, and it stands.

kit: A toolroll, and a contraption of your own making

callings.name: Gambler
callings.blurb: Every town past the railhead has a green-felt table and a soul who lives by it. The Gambler reads people the way the Prospector reads rock — the tell, the bluff, the breaking nerve — and has made a working peace with chance that most folk only pray for.

perk.name: Never a Stranger at the Table
perk.desc: Any game running in any town has a chair for you and credit enough to sit down with. By the time it breaks up you know what the table knows: who is flush, who is lying, who is leaving in the morning, and who owes money to the wrong man.

fight.brings: The dice themselves. Favor reaches into any roll at the table, yours or a foe's, and there is no round it cannot touch.
fight.costs: The thinnest Blood of any Worldly Calling, and a pool that empties whether the gamble paid or not. That is rather the point of it.

featureDescs.Fortune's Favor: Chance leans your way, and you have learned to lean back. Keep a pool of Favor equal to your PRE modifier + half your level (minimum 1), refreshed each dawn; you also recover 1 point whenever you stake something real on a genuine risk and let the dice fly. Spend a point to reroll any one d20 you just rolled and keep the better result, to add 1d6 to a check, or to force a foe to reroll a hit or a save made against you.
