perk.desc: What you pay for the dark shows on the world around you. Lamps gutter. Milk turns. The dog will not come into the room, and the priest's eye keeps coming back to you all through the sermon. Everyone in town knows what you are inside a week and not one of them can prove a word of it. You agreed to this.

fight.brings: The whole Old Dark ladder, earliest and deepest of anyone. Blood Price buys a working when the Nerve is gone.
fight.costs: The worst body in the book. A d6, a Slight attack, Backlash on everything, a Mark from the first day, and a price paid in your own Blood when the pool runs dry.

featureDescs.Signs: You know and may work Signs — the rites of the Old Dark (Chapter XIII) — drawing on the Common Signs and on the Bargain, the list of those who reached out and took. You begin knowing two and learn another at each even level, choosing freely from any Rank your level has opened to you. Working a Sign costs Nerve, and sometimes Blood, and always risks Backlash.
featureDescs.Witch-Sight: You see what is truly there: the residue of violence, the Mark upon a soul, the thin places where the world wears through. This sight cannot be unlearned, and some nights you wish it could.
featureDescs.Marked: You begin at Mark 1 and advance the Mark faster than others — reckless use of Signs, and the knowledge they bring, pushes you along the track toward the thing you are slowly becoming. Power and ruin are the same road.
featureDescs.Blood Price: From 5th level you may pay for a Sign in Blood (Hit Points) when your Nerve runs short, at a rate of 2 Blood per point of Nerve. The Old Dark does not care which red ledger you draw from.
featureDescs.Adept: At 10th level, choose one Sign you know. You may work it without spending Nerve once per scene — though never without consequence.
featureDescs.Working a Sign — the Short of It: Declare the Sign and pay its Nerve (or Blood). If it forces a save, the target rolls against your Sign DC = 10 + half your level + your RES modifier. Backlash strikes on the listed trigger — most often a natural 1 on any roll the working requires, or a failed working. The deep truths a Sign reveals may also demand a Dread Check of their own. Knowing is never free; for a Hexer, it is merely cheaper at first.
featureDescs.The Deeper Bargain: You may borrow against yourself. Once per scene, work any Sign you know without spending Nerve by instead taking its Nerve cost as damage that cannot be healed until you have slept. A Hexer who has learned this generally learns it in one particular night, and remembers that night for good.
featureDescs.Adept (Second): Choose a second Sign you know. It too may be worked once per scene without spending Nerve. The consequence attached to it does not stop attaching.
featureDescs.The Long Debt: Once per session, work any Sign of any rank you have ever read, whether or not you know it, whether or not you have the Nerve, at any scale the fiction can hold — a Sign laid on a town, on a river, on a bloodline, on a night. It works, completely, the first time and without a roll. Then the debt comes due, and it does not come due to you: the Keeper takes something from the world you were standing in. A person. A place. A year of somebody's life who never asked. You will be told what it cost afterward, in detail, and you will do it again, because you always know exactly what it is worth and you are never the one paying.

options.name: The Conjurer
options.boon: Bind a Sign or Rite into a charm anyone may trigger without Nerve (keep WIT-mod charms); +2 and half-time on Old Rites. Greater (9th): once per session, craft a great charm that wards a whole scene — allies gain a Ward, the uncanny recoil — paid for with something dear.

options.name: The Hollow-Born
options.boon: Feel pain and fear dimly — DR 2 vs nonmagical harm, ignore the first Nerve lost each scene — but advance the Mark faster. Greater (9th): at Mark 4+, once per scene work any Sign without Nerve, paying in Blood instead — each working a step nearer the sixth Mark.

options.name: The Pact-Sworn
options.boon: Once per scene, turn a failed Sign or Will save into a success by taking a Debt; on your third Debt the Patron calls it in — a demand, and +1 Mark. Greater (9th): once per session, when you would die, the Patron stays death's hand — stabilize at 1 Blood and rise, at the cost of +1 Mark.

options.name: The Spiritist
options.boon: See and briefly question the recently dead; set a willing spirit to watch and warn (+5 Notice). Greater (9th): once per session, invite a willing spirit to act through you for a round, borrowing a skill or memory; the unwilling risks possession.

callings.name: Witch
callings.blurb: Where the Hexer signs for borrowed power, the Witch was born to hers, or had it handed down a crooked family line, or learned it slow from an old woman at the edge of a town that no longer exists.

perk.name: They Come to You at Night
perk.desc: Whatever the town says about you in daylight, somebody knocks after dark: a girl in trouble, a man with a debt, a mother with a child that will not wake. You always have something worth trading, and there is always somebody in that town who cannot afford to watch you hang.

fight.brings: The Craft, which no other Calling may learn, a familiar out on the field with you, and the Evil Eye.
fight.costs: A d6 and the weakest Strike in the book. You will not shoot your way out of anything. The Craft is the whole of your answer and it is prepared work, so a fight you did not see coming is a fight you begin behind.

featureDescs.The Craft: You know and work Signs (Chapter XIII), beginning with two and learning another at each even level, paid in Nerve and risking Backlash as the Hexer's are, and choosing freely from any Rank your level has opened. Where you differ is the list. You draw on the Common Signs and on the Craft, and the Craft is closed to every other Calling in this book — no Hexer learns the Poppet, and no cultist will ever ward a house. The Craft is inherited, not borrowed: you do not begin Marked, and you advance the Mark only through genuine recklessness, never automatically. The dark did not hand you this. Your line did.
featureDescs.Familiar: A small beast is bound to you — a cat, a crow, a hare, a toad, a black snake. It is cannier than any animal, scouts and spies at your bidding, can deliver a touch-range Sign for you, and grants a standing boon while near (a +2 to one sense or skill befitting its nature). You share its senses at will. Should it die, you are Sickened until you can bind another over a long night's rite — and you will feel the loss far longer than the penalty lasts.
featureDescs.The Evil Eye: With a look and a muttered word, lay a minor bane on a creature you can see (Will save vs your Sign DC): –1 to its rolls and a run of small misfortunes for a round per two levels. It costs no Nerve, but everyone who sees you do it remembers your face.
featureDescs.Brew: This is the kitchen craft, not the Rank 3 Sign of the same family — The Brewing bottles a working, while this bottles medicine. Given a kitchen, a fire, and time, you brew the work of the Goods chapter and more — healing poultices, sleeping draughts, truth-loosening teas, and poisons that no assayer can name. Treat your brews as a Sawbones' Tonics, with effects you and the Keeper devise; the dose is in the making, and the making is in your hands.
featureDescs.Hex: Your maledictions grow teeth. As an action and 1 Nerve, lay a true Hex on a foe (Will save vs Sign DC): Frightened, Clumsy, Sickened, or cursed with ruinous luck (foes' crits against allies, your crits against the cursed) for a scene. A Hexed soul knows it is Hexed, and knows who did it, which is sometimes the worst of it.
featureDescs.The Old Witch: At 10th level your curses set like winter ground: a target who fails a Hex carries it until it is lifted by rite, apology, or your death. Once per session you may speak a true curse of dire and lasting effect, the kind that follows a bloodline. You have outlived everyone who feared you young. The ones who fear you now are right to.
featureDescs.Witch and Hexer — the Difference: Both work Signs and pay in Nerve, but the Hexer's power is a loan (begins Marked, races the Mark) while the Witch's is inheritance (no starting Mark, advances it only through abuse). A Hexer can become a Witch's cautionary tale; a Witch can become a Hexer the day she reaches for something her line never taught her. Keep the distinction at the table — it is the whole tragedy of the chapter.
featureDescs.The Second Familiar: A second beast comes to you and stays. Bind it as you bound the first, from the table of familiars: you gain its boon as well, both may be abroad at once, and either may carry the Evil Eye for you at a distance you can walk in an hour. Two of them will not stay in the same room, and you will spend a surprising amount of your life managing that.
featureDescs.The Deep Craft: Your brews and hexes have stopped being small. A Brew you make lasts a season rather than a day and may be given away without weakening, and a Hex you lay may name a condition for its lifting rather than a duration — a spoken apology, a returned thing, a river crossed, a name said three times. Most who carry one never learn the condition, which is generally the point.
featureDescs.What the Old Ones Knew: Once per session, do the thing the old women in the stories do. Change one thing that has already happened this session, as though it had gone otherwise: the shot missed, the door was locked, the letter never came, she was somewhere else that night. It is not an illusion and nobody remembers it the old way except you and anything older than you. The world simply is as you have said. What it costs is fixed: you age a year, the nearest living thing that trusts you dies quietly within the week, and one of your own memories goes into the gap to hold it open. You will not know which one is missing. You will only notice, sometimes, that there is a space where a name used to be.

options.name: The Cursewife
options.boon: Your Hexes and Evil Eye strike harder and cling tighter; Hex two targets at once; lifting your curse costs dearly. Greater (9th): once per session, lay a curse of escalating ruin on a wrongdoer until they amend, fall, or flee the country.

options.name: The Familiar-Bound
options.boon: Your familiar grows clever and hardy, delivers your Signs, and lets you see and hear through it at any distance. Greater (9th): swap places with it once per scene and share wounds or Blood; should you fall, it carries your spirit to a new dawn — once.

options.name: The Greenwitch
options.boon: Brews never spoil and take half the time; keep a free healing or warding brew; +2 Survival and Medicine; beasts will not harm you unbidden. Greater (9th): once per scene, call the wild — walling thorns, a healing green circle, or a trail the land hides until dawn.

options.name: The Moon-Daughter
options.boon: See in the dark; once a night take to the air until dawn; slip into a sleeper's dreams to glean or leave a secret. Greater (9th): once per session, ride the night sky to any place you have been, carrying your coven, and walk the dreams of the distant sleeping.

hungerLadder.1: The want has a shape now, and you know its name
hungerLadder.2: Cold to the touch; you stop bothering to pretend at meals
hungerLadder.3: Your Shape's tell shows plainly, and will not be explained away twice
hungerLadder.4: Dogs will not abide you; the living find reasons to sit elsewhere
hungerLadder.5: You are mostly want. Will save to refuse what is put in front of you
hungerLadder.6: You are Consumed; the character passes into the Keeper's hands
